extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of psychology, psychoanalysis, literary theory, and humor studies; readers studying the psychology of wit
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying Freud's psychoanalytic criteria for how witticisms are formed and how they function (techniques, psychic origins, social constraints, and categories of wit). Useful for analysing or producing witty/comic material from a psychoanalytic/literary perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation (wit-technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Condensation is a central technique shared by dream-work and wit: multiple elements are fused or compressed into a single expression, producing brevity and intensified elements while others are lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freud links condensation to the brevity and striking character of witticisms; condensation can lead to manifold application of the same material, play upon words, and similarity of sound. It originates in the unconscious and may strengthen some elements while others become lost. In practice, look for compressed expressions, puns, and fused associations as evidence of condensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displacement (shift of psychic emphasis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Displacement manifests when what is prominent in the manifest utterance occupies a peripheral position in the underlying thought, and vice versa; psychic energy passes from important to insignificant ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In dreams displacement is extensive and allows objectionable elements to pass the censor; in wit displacement also appears but is usually restricted by requirements of intelligibility. Displacement can produce deviation of trend, indirect allusions, and substitutions (symbols, comparisons, trifles). It is a tool for overcoming inhibition but must remain decipherable in social wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect representation / allusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of allusion, symbol, comparison, or indirect substitution to express something objectionable or to enhance wit without stating it directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allusion in wit may be either intentionally constructed (non-witty) or spontaneous (witty). Witty allusions typically arise without conscious preparatory stages. In contrast to dream-work's exaggeration of indirect expression, wit uses indirect representation within bounds that a third person can understand. Beware of forced, over-extended allusions that feel 'forced' rather than genuinely witty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity as a hallmark
rubrics_metrics.description: Peculiar brevity is a marked and distinctive characteristic of wit, arising from unconscious condensation rather than mere economizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brevity of a joke often produces a striking impression and is tied to the localization of associations in the unconscious. Expect witticisms to be concise; verbosity often dilutes the wit. However brevity alone does not guarantee wit—its effect depends on condensation and associative payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit as involuntary inspiration (sudden flash)
rubrics_metrics.description: Witticisms typically appear as sudden, involuntary 'inspirations' — a flash of thought that emerges without deliberate, fully conscious construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freud contrasts this with purposeful allusion-making: intentionally formed allusions are not usually witty. In practice, spontaneous-seeming timing and a subjective sense of a sudden drop in intellectual tension often accompany genuine wit. Attempts to will a joke often produce sterile, non-witty allusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unconscious / infantile source
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit draws on unconscious processes that are fundamentally infantile in character; the unconscious mental processes reproduce the 'playing' mentality of childhood that delights in word-play and nonsense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freud argues the infantile is the source of the unconscious, so wit reactivates childhood play with words to produce pleasure. Recognize 'childish' or playful mechanisms (repetition, simple puns, neat reversals) as signs of this origin, and note how they evoke a pleasurable, 'childlike' response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the censor / inhibition overcoming
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit must overcome an inhibiting force (the 'censor'); techniques of wit serve to bypass, soften, or circumvent objections from critical reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where dreams rely heavily on displacement to evade the censor, wit more often uses ambiguity, double-meaning, or a context in which a potentially offensive element can be simultaneously admissible. When analyzing or producing wit, identify how the expression negotiates social or internal prohibitions—either by substitution, ambiguity, or timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-sidedness / 'sense in nonsense' (ambiguity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit commonly presents a double-sided quality: nonsense or apparent meaninglessness that simultaneously yields a sensible (or jocular) reading — 'sense in nonsense.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This double-dealing is central to wit's ability to be both permissible and pleasurable. The ambiguity (semantic, phonetic, or associative) enables the same utterance to satisfy censorship yet deliver an illicit or pleasurable meaning. Use and value ambiguity, but ensure the alternate reading is recoverable by the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social intelligibility and third-person condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit is a social psychic function that demands intelligibility to at least one other person (often a third person) and therefore must limit the degree of concealment or disfigurement used in expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike dreams (asocial, disguised), wit must be decipherable by a listener; excessive obscurity or dream-like disfigurement will make a joke fail. When crafting wit, constrain techniques (condensation/displacement) so the audience can decode the underlying thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony and representation through the opposite
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation through the opposite (saying the reverse of what one means) underlies irony; it requires signals (inflection, gesture, style) that indicate the intended contrary meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irony presupposes the listener's readiness to hear a contradiction; it risks misunderstanding if the audience does not recognize the cue. It also helps avoid direct invective while producing comic pleasure by eliciting an anticipated contradiction that turns out unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonsense / absurdity as purposeful device
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonsense and absurdity are not accidental in wit but can be purposely admitted by the wit-work to express scorn, criticism, or to enhance psychic discharge and comic pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonsensical façades increase the psychic expenditure in the hearer and the amount discharged through laughter. While caricature/parody/travesty can produce comical nonsense without invoking unconscious processes, wit's nonsense frequently serves both expressive and pleasure-producing ends and may reactivate infantile pleasures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from dream-technique (limits on displacement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although wit and dream-work share many techniques (condensation, displacement, indirect expression), wit restricts these to the limits of conscious intelligibility; dreams freely exceed such bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where dream-analyses may seem 'witty' to outsiders (because of remote associations and extreme disfigurement), genuine wit must keep substitutions and displacements within decipherable limits. Use dream analogies cautiously when interpreting or creating wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed formation stages of wit (foreconscious → unconscious → conscious)
rubrics_metrics.description: Freud's formula: a foreconscious thought is left for a moment to unconscious elaboration and the results are then grasped by conscious perception; analogous to stages of dream-formation but without regression to perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a hypothesized psychic process for the first-person formation of wit. In analysis or creative practice, consider that the best phrasing for an idea may arise after letting a thought 'drop' from conscious control, allowing associative processes to generate condensed/ambiguous formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection via unconscious elaboration (choice of expression)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exact expression that yields the gain in word-pleasure is often selected unconsciously; lowering occupation energy to the unconscious permits associative paths that favor witty formulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consciously hunting for phrasing is usually less effective; techniques that facilitate associative drift (relaxation, playful mood) can help produce superior wit. Evaluate whether an utterance seems the product of associative selection rather than deliberate assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of wit: jest, harmless wit, tendency-wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Different stages/types of wit have different psychic dispositions: the 'jest' originates in a happy mood and lowers psychic energies; 'harmless wit' pairs wit with a valuable thought and depends on personal adaptation; 'tendency-wit' serves unconscious tendencies and is driven by strong unconscious motives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying or producing wit, identify which category applies: jests are mood-dependent and widely accessible; harmless wit requires a personal knack or adaptation; tendency-wit often reflects deeper unconscious or aggressive impulses and may correlate with neurotic tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of outer associations (sound/contiguity) as substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: The substitution of inner associations (similarity, causal) by outer associations (simultaneity, contiguity in space, assonance) is characteristic of dream-work and occurs in wit as a source/object of pleasure (e.g., puns, phonetic play).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for and value phonetic or surface-level associations (rhyme, assonance, spatial/temporal contiguity) that substitute for deeper logical associations and produce comic effect. But ensure such substitutions remain intelligible to listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naïve comic (comic discovered in others' uninhibited behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'naïve' comic arises not from making but from finding the comical in others who are uninhibited; it cannot be deliberately produced and depends on perceiving someone lacking inhibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between wit (made) and the naïve comic (found). In social comedy analysis, recognize that laughs at naïveté stem from perceiving absence of inhibition in another, and producing such situations intentionally risks being judged impudent rather than comical.
